subject.title: Guard Telegram and iMessage dispatch against fleet loops

question: Should Telegram/iMessage loop suppression be implemented as OpenClaw-owned channel or turn admission, or may this PR introduce a host-local external `fleet-loop-guard` subprocess in shared provider dispatch?
rationale: The current patch changes a shared dispatch security boundary and availability behavior; automation cannot choose that product/security contract safely.

options.title: Move To Owned Admission
options.body: Implement the loop check in OpenClaw-owned channel or turn admission before session record and dispatch, reusing the existing pair-loop guard where possible.

options.title: Accept External Helper Contract
options.body: Keep the subprocess approach only if maintainers explicitly document installation, versioning, timeout, data-sharing, and operator security expectations.

options.title: Pause Or Close This Branch
options.body: Pause or close this branch if the fleet-specific helper is not a core contract and a narrower Telegram/iMessage API should be designed first.

recommendation.title: Move To Owned Admission
recommendation.body: Implement the loop check in OpenClaw-owned channel or turn admission before session record and dispatch, reusing the existing pair-loop guard where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current generic bot-loop protection seam and is the strongest history match for deciding whether this belongs in core turn admission.
